initial_rank_interpretation.uncorrected_versions: For any fixed transform, shared initial right-specialist states make all 15 candidate scores analytically tied. Initial rank 1 is not unique identification. At identity the score is self-CKA 1 whenever defined.
initial_rank_interpretation.dual_answer_residual_identity: All 15 candidates remain analytically tied at self-CKA 1 because each pair residualizes two equal states with the same design. Exact floating-point rank deviations can be roundoff.
initial_rank_interpretation.dual_answer_residual_nonidentity: Pair-specific additive answer designs can change initial scores/ranks despite identical initial specialist parameters; such initial ranks do not evidence learned specialist information.
initial_rank_interpretation.bounded_numerical_audit: The separate three-case identity audit observed a single-length ordinary U-CKA roundoff rank 13 for valleys, despite identical arrays and a mathematical 15-way tie. It did not find residual identity deviations.

narrow_conclusion: A positive residual strongest-alternative advantage survives fixed-length additive-answer control on average and in many cells, with substantial encoding/configuration dependence and genuine negative cells. The result is not solely one task pair, but does not establish universal relations, a mathematical mechanism, complete removal of answer information, or functional benefit. The large initialization-relative increase largely reflects reduced identity similarity from the shared initialization, while mean designated CKA decreases.
